Quick start

agetime.Rmd

Working with age group, period, and cohort labels is often awkward and error-prone. The agetime package makes it easier. This vignette introduces some of the basic functions. The vignette focuses on age group labels, but equivalent functions also exist for period and cohort labels.

Infer intervals from labels

Given a vector of age group labels, extract lower limits, upper limits, midpoints, and widths:

library(agetime)

x <- c("0", "1-4", "5-9", "10+")
age_lower(x)
#>   0 1-4 5-9 10+ 
#>   0   1   5  10
age_upper(x)
#>   0 1-4 5-9 10+ 
#>   1   5  10 Inf
age_mid(x)
#>    0  1-4  5-9  10+ 
#>  0.5  3.0  7.5 12.0
age_width(x)
#>   0 1-4 5-9 10+ 
#>   1   4   5 Inf

Use the lower limit to filter rows:

library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

df <- tibble(
  age   = c("0-14", "15-64", "65+"),
  count = c(100, 200, 50)
)

df |>
  filter(age_lower(age) >= 15)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   age   count
#>   <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 15-64   200
#> 2 65+      50

Find special labels

agetime knows about totals and open intervals.

df <- tibble(
  age   = c("15-64", "0-14", "65+", "All"),
  count = c(5, 2, 6, 13)
)

df |>
  filter(!age_is_total(age))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   age   count
#>   <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 15-64     5
#> 2 0-14      2
#> 3 65+       6

df |>
  filter(age_is_open_right(age))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   age   count
#>   <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 65+       6

Standardize messy labels

age_standard() converts labels to a standard format:

x <- c("5to9", "10--14", "100plus")
age_standard(x)
#> [1] "5-9"   "10-14" "100+"

Create a regular series of labels

The age_labels functions generate labels from scratch.

age_labels_five(lower_first = 0, lower_last = 20)
#> [1] "0-4"   "5-9"   "10-14" "15-19" "20+"
age_labels_life(lower_last = 60) ## life table age groups
#>  [1] "0"     "1-4"   "5-9"   "10-14" "15-19" "20-24" "25-29" "30-34" "35-39"
#> [10] "40-44" "45-49" "50-54" "55-59" "60+"

Manipulate levels

Use the age_coarsen functions to convert to wider age groups.

x <- c("0-4", "5-9", "10-14", "50-54")
age_coarsen(x, breaks = c(0, 15, 55))
#> [1] 0-14  0-14  0-14  15-54
#> Levels: 0-14 15-54
age_coarsen_five(x)
#> [1] "0-4"   "5-9"   "10-14" "50-54"

Use the age_fill functions to add intermediate levels:

x |>
  age_coarsen_five() |>
  age_fill_five()
#> [1] 0-4   5-9   10-14 50-54
#> Levels: 0-4 5-9 10-14 15-19 20-24 25-29 30-34 35-39 40-44 45-49 50-54

Check and assert

Check whether age labels conform to expectations:

lab <- age_labels_five(
  lower_first = 0,
  lower_last = 85,
  open_right = TRUE
)
age_diagnose(
  lab,
  no_overlap = TRUE,
  no_gap = TRUE,
  has_zero = TRUE,
  has_open_right = TRUE
)
#> $ok
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   condition      passed comment
#>   <chr>          <lgl>  <chr>  
#> 1 no_overlap     TRUE   NA     
#> 2 no_gap         TRUE   NA     
#> 3 has_zero       TRUE   NA     
#> 4 has_open_right TRUE   NA

age_assert() throws an error if a check fails.

Create mappings

age_mapping() builds a mapping between sets of labels.

labels_x <- c("10--14", "0--9")
labels_y <- c("0-4", "5-9", "10-14")
age_mapping(
  labels_x,
  labels_y,
  relation = "contains",
  format = "matrix"
)
#>         y
#> x        0-4 5-9 10-14
#>   10--14   0   0     1
#>   0--9     1   1     0

Period and cohort

Age group functions have period and cohort equivalents. For instance:

Age Period Cohort
age_lower() period_lower() cohort_lower()
age_standard() period_standard() cohort_standard()
age_labels_five() period_labels_five() cohort_labels_five()
age_coarsen() period_coarsen() cohort_coarsen()

Function tasks

agetime functions fall into five groups, defined by their tasks:

Task Examples Return value
Extract limits or identify special labels age_lower(), age_upper(), age_mid(), age_width(), age_is_total() Numeric or logical
Create a new series, or reformat existing labels age_labels_five(), age_standard(), age_extend() Character, or same type as labels
Recode values and set factor levels age_coarsen(), age_fill(), age_set_open_right(), age_set_order() Factor
Validate labels age_diagnose(), age_assert() Diagnostics, or labels
Relate two sets of labels age_mapping() Tibble or matrix
